papers.title: Uncertainty-Aware Machine Learning for NBA Forecasting in Digital Betting Markets
papers.key_result: LR + XGBoost with Monte Carlo Dropout and isotonic calibration achieves Brier ~0.20 on 2024 NBA season. Isotonic post-processing is the key calibration step.
papers.relevance: DIRECT — confirms calibration is the bridge from tree-model Brier ~0.22 to target ~0.20

papers.title: Stacked ensemble model for NBA game outcome prediction analysis
papers.key_result: Stacked ensembles (NB + AdaBoost + MLP + KNN + XGBoost + DT + LR) for outcome prediction. Diversity in base learners improves ensemble calibration.
papers.relevance: MEDIUM — ensemble diversity aligns with our multi-island GA approach; stacking as post-GA step

papers.title: Comparative Evaluation of Machine Learning Models for NBA Game Outcome Prediction
papers.key_result: CNN achieved Brier 0.221. SVM accuracy 0.7749. Fleet already beats CNN Brier benchmark (fleet best 0.22062).
papers.relevance: CONTEXT — confirms fleet is at/above SOTA for tree-based models without calibration

proposed_implementation.target_island: S22 (TESTforge42/nba-evo-s22) — most stable, gen 2552, stagnation 0 post-reset
implementation_plan: 1. In app.py: after model.fit() in evaluate_model(), wrap: calibrated = CalibratedClassifierCV(model, method='isotonic', cv='prefit'); calibrated.fit(X_val, y_val)
2. Use calibrated.predict_proba() instead of model.predict_proba() for Brier evaluation
3. Hold-out calibration set: last 2 seasons (2024-25, 2025-26) — never seen during GA evolution
4. A/B compare: raw Brier vs calibrated Brier on same feature set
5. If calibrated_brier < raw_brier - 0.001, adopt calibration in final evaluation; else revert
proposed_implementation.risk: LOW — isotonic calibration is monotone transformation, cannot increase Brier below random
